quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: An orange and red triangular sign on a vehicle means:

options.text: The vehicle has the right-of-way.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Road work ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: Slow-moving vehicles like farm tractors, road maintenance vehicles, and animal-drawn carts display an orange and red triangle on the back.

questions.question: A broken yellow line down the center of a road means:

options.text: Construction is ahead.
You cannot pass from either direction.
You can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means any driver may pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A blood alcohol level of 0.02 percent:

options.text: Will not affect your driving.
Will not put other drivers at risk.
Will double your chance of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will double your chance of having an accident.
questions.explanation: For every 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol, a driver's risk of a fatal crash nearly doubles.

questions.question: This yellow sign means:

options.text: The road ahead has many curves.
There is a sharp curve ahead.
The road ahead may be slippery.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead may be slippery.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road ahead may be slippery when wet.

questions.question: A red arrow pointing right on a traffic light means you may:

options.text: Turn in that direction after slowing and checking for traffic.
Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.
Turn in that direction after you come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must wait until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog. They help other drivers see you, even if they don't help you see much better.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, you may go in the direction of the arrow if:

options.text: You come to a complete stop first.
You wait until the light changes.
You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: If you are in a lane with a green arrow, you may go in that direction when it is safe. This applies whether the arrow is alone or with another signal.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, you should:

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
Expect all drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Drive close to the parked cars to give more room for moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly enter your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep distance between your car and parked cars. A person may step out without looking. A driver may start moving before seeing you.

questions.question: When should you return to your original lane after passing?

options.text: When you feel you are far enough ahead.
When the other driver signals you to return.
When you can see the other car's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the other car's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Use your right turn signal before returning to the right lane. It is safe to return when you can see the entire car you passed in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: When pulling into traffic from a parked position, you should:

options.text: Drive slower than other traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a gap large enough to reach the speed of traffic.
Wait for the first two vehicles to pass, then enter the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a gap large enough to reach the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, wait for a large enough gap so your car can reach the same speed as other traffic.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A solid line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit on a state road when no other speed is posted?

options.text: 70 mph.
55 mph.
40 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 55 mph.
questions.explanation: The speed limit on state roads is 55 mph unless a different speed limit is posted. Follow the posted speed limit if one is shown.

questions.question: When can you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Do not drive around or under a lowered gate at any railroad crossing. Wait until the gate is raised. Then check both directions and make sure no trains are coming before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: If you are following a school bus or tank truck, what should you do?

options.text: Pass them on the right.
Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.
Drive closer behind them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: School buses and tank trucks with hazardous materials must stop at all railroad crossings. Always be prepared to stop if you are following one of these vehicles.

questions.question: You are exiting the freeway on a curved ramp that goes downhill. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down to a safe speed before entering the curve.
Slow down to the posted freeway speed limit.
Wait until you are in the curve to start braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to a safe speed before entering the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You cannot see what is ahead. Braking inside a curve can cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: Where are a truck's blind spots?

options.text: Directly behind the body.
On the left side near the cab.
On the left side near the cab and directly behind the body.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side near the cab and directly behind the body.
questions.explanation: Trucks have very large blind spots. The driver cannot see vehicles behind or to the left of the truck. If you cannot see the driver's face in their side mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: When passing another car, when is it safe to return to the driving lane?

options.text: When the other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.
When you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.
When you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You need a safe gap between your vehicle and the passed vehicle before returning to the driving lane. When you can see both headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to move back.

questions.question: You are on the freeway behind a large truck. How should you drive?

options.text: Close behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead.
Farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
No more than one car length behind so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely behind a truck, the driver cannot see you. Tailgating removes your safety cushion if the truck stops suddenly.

questions.question: How can you see vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Check the inside rearview mirror.
Check the outside rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. You must look over your shoulders to check them.

questions.question: You should allow extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Allow extra space when following a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop faster than most vehicles. You need room to stop if the rider brakes or falls. Also, motorcycles are hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this road sign?

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign means a divided highway is starting. Stay in the right lane.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches you?

options.text: Pull over to the right side of the road and stop completely.
Keep driving, but try to get out of its way.
Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: The law requires you to move over for police cars, fire trucks, and ambulances with flashing lights and sirens. Pull to the right edge of the road as far as possible. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Driving aggressively.
Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
More dangerous than regular driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means using safe strategies to prevent crashes. You adjust your driving based on weather, how you feel, and what other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians do.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and crash severity relate to vehicle speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights. If visibility is too poor, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is safe.
Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
Speed does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous because drivers behind you may become frustrated and make risky passes. Drive with the flow of traffic within the speed limit.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lane markings mean?

options.text: Neither lane may pass.
Both lanes may pass.
The right lane may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Neither lane may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow markings separate lanes with traffic moving in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: What should you do when driving near a large commercial truck?

options.text: Follow it closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots on each side. Do not drive beside them for long periods of time.

questions.question: How should you make a right turn?

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the center line before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Approach in the right lane, then move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Signal before turning to warn other drivers. Slow down and use the right lane, staying as close to the right curb as safely possible.

questions.question: What are "No zones" around trucks?

options.text: Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop and steer safely.
Safe areas behind the truck.
Areas with several car lengths between your vehicle and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop and steer safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are blind spots around trucks or buses where cars cannot be seen. They are also areas where cars are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or steer safely. Staying in a "No zone" greatly increases crash risk.
